title: Spotlight warmup lattice and tenant floor — PRD draft
body:
Summary:

This draft proposes the "Spotlight Warmup Lattice" (SWL) and Tenant Floor constructs to improve Dedicated capacity behavior for short-duration microbursts, long-running sustained ramps, and noisy neighbors. SWL is a layered warmup system that gives priority windows ("spotlights") to tenants who signal imminent load, while Tenant Floor guarantees a minimum compute baseline per committed customer. Combined with a soft-fidelity-swap and a bounded handoff-margin, this design aims to: reduce cold-start latency for bursty traffic, avoid wholesale eviction during demand spikes, and preserve predictable latency SLOs for committed tenants.

Problem statement and context:

Current Dedicated pool behavior suffers across three axes:
- Microburst cold-starts: customers with bursty traffic experience 200–800ms additional tail latency during container/gpu warmup.
- Noisy neighbors: sudden throughput surges from opportunistic tenants can starve SLO-sensitive customers.
- Coarse burst accounting: our existing credit/reservation model is binary (reserve vs burst) and forces blunt eviction or admission decisions, leading to customer surprise and operational toil.

We need a mechanism that is operationally simple for customers to reason about, low friction to adopt, and that gracefully degrades workload fidelity rather than forcing hard evictions.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce median cold-start token latency for 95th-percentile burst events by 40% within 90 days of rollout.
- Keep committed-tenant 99th-percentile latency within SLA during 95% of detected burst windows.
- Reduce number of manual dedicated-pool escalations from capacity spikes by 60% (quarterly).
- Maintain <=5% monthly additional infra cost due to warm pools across high-utilization clusters.

Non-goals:
- Replace existing dedicated-credit economy completely (this is an additive capability).
- Solve arbitrary multi-region disaster scenarios in first iteration.

Design overview (high level):

1) Spotlight Warmup Lattice (SWL)
- Concept: SWL defines short-lived, small-capacity warm pockets (spotlights) that can be dynamically provisioned for tenants who provide a lightweight pre-warm signal (see API below). Spotlights are layered in a lattice of priority: Top spotlights (for high-SLA tenants) have faster pre-warm paths and lower admission latency; lower spotlights are opportunistic.
- Mechanics: when a tenant signals an upcoming burst (n seconds), the orchestrator attempts to allocate a spotlight slot from a local warm pool. If available, the spotlight binds a fraction of a GPU (vCPU/GPU-slice) and populates KV cache and model weights. The spotlight is timeboxed (default 120s) and will convert to sustained allocation only if burst continues and Tenant Floor economics permit.
- Size & placement: spotlight slots are small (e.g., 2–8 concurrent concurrency units, configurable per tenant class) and should preferentially reuse warm instances on the same host to preserve cache locality.

2) Tenant Floor
- Concept: a soft-minimum compute guarantee for committed customers (monthly reserved capacity). Tenant Floor is expressed as a percentile throughput floor (e.g., 50 rps or X tokens/s) and is enforced by priority admission and protected spotlights.
- Enforcement: when contention occurs, scheduler reduces spotlight/opportunistic lanes first, then preemptible slots, preserving Tenant Floor. Floors are negotiated at reservation time and appear in the customer console as a numeric baseline plus a latency target.

3) Hand-off Margin and Reconciliation
- Concept: to avoid hard failovers when a spotlight is borrowed or converted to sustained capacity, we introduce a "handoff-margin": a bounded borrowing allowance (e.g., up to 20% of a tenant's committed floor for short windows) with an accounting ledger that reconciles usage at billing/settlement.
- Safety: handoff-margin borrowing is rate-limited and time-limited (max continuous 10 minutes), and requires downstream signals to avoid cascading depletion (backpressure + telemetry validation).

4) Soft-fidelity-swap
- Concept: instead of evicting traffic outright under severe pressure, we provide configurable fidelity degrade paths per tenant: lighter model quantization, shorter gen lengths, or fallback to cached completions. Degrades are annotated in response metadata and reversible.

APIs and tenant UX (sketch):
- Pre-warm signal (lightweight): POST /v1/dedicated/prewarm { "tenant_id": "T-123", "window_s": 30, "priority": "spotlight" }
- Floor negotiation appears on console when creating/renewing reservations: "floor_tokens_per_sec" and "floor_latency_ms_p99"
- Visibility: new console tab "Warmup & Floors" showing active spotlights, time remaining, and handoff ledger. Alerts for reconciliation anomalies (e.g., unaccounted handoff > threshold).

Scheduler behavior (pseudo flow):
1. Receive prewarm signal; check local warm pool for free spotlight slots.
2. If free, allocate spotlight (populate caches), mark as reserved for Xs.
3. If no free local slots, attempt cross-host spotlight pin (lower priority).
4. If still none, consider ephemeral spin-up (if cold-start cost < penalty) or respond with estimated warm latency to caller.
5. On sustained high load, convert spotlight to sustained allocation if Tenant Floor and handoff-margin allow; else trigger fidelity-swap and queue advisory to tenant.

Operational runbook (ops-ready summary):
- Detection: SWL emits events when warm pools drop below threshold or when handoff debt crosses 60%.
- Auto-remediation: automated reprovisioning of warm pools across nodes based on heatmaps; temporary widening of spotlights to absorb bursts under low cluster utilization.
- Paging: on handoff ledger anomalies (e.g., >2 tenants borrowing >50% their floor concurrently), page SRE with playbook "swl-handback": revert spotlight conversions and activate fidelity-swap lane.

Cost model & billing reconciliation:
- Spotlights are cheaper per-minute than full dedicated reservation but have a small premium over pure burst usage because of warm pool residency cost.
- Handoff-margin borrowing is tracked as ledger entries; event-level reconciliation occurs daily and is surfaced as usage delta on invoice. Finance/Revenue teams will map handoff usage to soft credits or billable units depending on contract.

Observability and telemetry:
- New metrics: spotlight_alloc_rate, spotlight_success_rate, handoff_debt, tenant_floor_breaches, fidelity_swap_count.
- Dashboards: per-pool heatmap, tenant-level warm success, and a reconciliation report for billed vs ledgerled handoff.

Safety and edge cases:
- Misuse: noisy tenants issuing repeated prewarm signals could bloat warm pools. Mitigation: tokenized prewarm budget per tenant, backoff windows, and cost-based throttling enforced in the control plane.
- Multi-tenant cache thrash: prefer spotlight reuse and host affinity; fall back to disk cache or compressed KV if thrash observed.
- Cross-region signals: prewarm is local only; for cross-region warmup we surface a warning and provide estimate times.

Implementation roadmap (quarterly slices):
- Q1 (prototype): lightweight prewarm API, local spotlight scheduler, warm-pool microservice, basic console surface. Experiment on two dev clusters.
- Q2 (pilot): Tenant Floor proposal on 5 pilot customers, handoff-margin ledger, billing reconciliation prototype, basic fidelity-swap hooks.
- Q3 (scale): broader rollout to 25% Dedicated fleets with autoscale signals driving warm pool sizing, SLO alarms.
- Q4 (polish): regional warm balancing, configurable fidelity-swap policies per tenant, formal SLA updates and pricing artifacts.

Metrics to evaluate success (examples):
- Reduction in cold-start latency for pre-warmed requests (p50/p95/p99).
- Fraction of bursts fully absorbed by spotlight without fidelity-swap.
- Handback debt outstanding and reconciliation latency.
- Customer reported incidents related to evictions.

Open questions & tradeoffs:
1. How large should default spotlight slots be? (2–8 concurrency units is initial guess). Need perf experiments across model families.
2. Billing semantics: should handoff-margin be billable immediately or reconciled monthly? Finance preference required.
3. Security: does cross-tenant warm pool reuse introduce data leakage risk? (We believe not if process isolation + salt per-tenant caches maintained; security review required.)
4. UX clarity: how do we present probabilistic warm guarantees without confusing customers? Need controlled language and examples in console.

Appendix: short experiment plan
- Run A/B: on dev cluster A enable SWL prewarm for selected tenants; cluster B baseline. Simulate 10k microbursts/day, measure cold-start delta, spotlight hit rate, and fidelity-swap triggers.
- Perf matrix: run across gtx-family models, Llama2/Redwood-medium and quantized variants to measure warm residency memory overhead and average spin-up time.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally opinionated: SWL combines operational shortcuts (small warm pools) with conservative economics (handoff ledger) to avoid changing our whole credit model. If reviewers prefer a pure-market model (auctioning spotlights), note that adds complexity for initial launch and likely increases latency for buyers.
- Please review linked eng ticket ENG-4321 for scheduler proto and the infra PR that adds warm-pool service.

Action items for next week:
- Marco: perf microbench for 3 model families (due 2025-01-20).
- Aisha: draft UI copy for "Warmup & Floors" console (due 2025-01-24).
- Kenji: security checklist and isolation threat model (due 2025-01-27).
- Priya: finalize pilot customer list and update pilot SOW draft (due 2025-01-30).

---
Informal notes (brainstorm fragments):
- Consider "credit escrow" where marketplace-like lending ensures spotlights are fungible across tenants with opt-in pooling.
- Long-tail thought: use model-splitting (serve heads on tiny CPU containers while GPU warms) to reduce perceived latency; requires frontend changes.
- Keep console simple: show 3 numbers: active spotlights, floor utilization, and handoff debt.

End of draft.
